basis: Drafted from 80 design-split comments (redacted text only); the test and calibration splits were not read. Examples below are paraphrased, not customer text. themes-2 (30 Oct) sharpened theme boundaries after calibration review: no label space change.

overall_sentiment.mixed: At least one favourable and one unfavourable point.
overall_sentiment.neutral: No clear favourable or unfavourable point (for example a bare fact or an unclear note).

communication.label: Communication and follow-up
communication.definition: Updates during the job, returning calls or messages, passing messages on, responsiveness to enquiries.
examples: Had to ring three times for an update.
They texted me at each step.

timeliness.label: Timeliness and waiting
timeliness.definition: Speed of service, waiting or queueing, finishing when promised, part or car ready on the agreed day.
examples: Promised by noon, collected at five.
In and out within the hour.

staff_attitude.label: Staff attitude
staff_attitude.definition: Friendliness, courtesy, helpfulness, respect and effort of the people involved.
examples: Lovely team at the front desk.
The salesperson was dismissive.

explanation.label: Explanation and advice
explanation.definition: How clearly work, invoices, options or vehicle features were explained, including handover education such as charging an EV.
examples: Each item on the invoice was explained.
Nobody showed me how to use the charger.

price_value.label: Price and value
price_value.definition: Price level, fairness or value for money (not unexpected or unapproved charges, which are billing).
examples: Cheaper than I expected.
Too expensive for what was done.

billing.label: Billing accuracy
billing.definition: Charges that differ from the quote, unapproved add-ons, unexplained fees or invoice errors.
examples: An extra fee appeared that nobody mentioned.
Paid more than the quote.

work_quality.label: Work quality
work_quality.definition: Whether the repair or service was done correctly: fault not fixed, damage, missed steps, rework.
examples: Same noise is still there.
A cover was left unclipped.

parts_availability.label: Parts availability
parts_availability.definition: Whether parts or accessories were in stock or obtainable.
examples: Part out of stock again.
They had it on the shelf.

sales_pressure.label: Sales pressure
sales_pressure.definition: Pushing finance, insurance, extended warranties or other add-ons, or pressure to buy.
examples: Forty minutes of insurance pitch.
No pushy upselling at all.

process_ease.label: Ease of process
process_ease.definition: How easy booking, drop-off, paperwork or the purchase process was overall.
examples: Booking took three calls.
Smooth and hassle-free from start to finish.

vehicle_handover.label: Vehicle readiness at handover
vehicle_handover.definition: Whether a sold vehicle was ready, complete and clean at delivery: missing items, not prepared, not ready on time for collection.
examples: Spare key and mats were missing.
Car was detailed and ready to go.

rules: Assign every theme the comment supports; a comment can have several themes, and the same theme cannot be both positive and negative.
Judge the meaning, not single words: sarcasm such as 'Oh brilliant, another day of silence' is negative.
A purely generic remark ('Top job', 'Welcoming') takes staff_attitude only when it describes the people; otherwise use overall sentiment with no theme.
Placeholders such as [NAME] or [REGO] are redactions; ignore them.
Some comments are staff notes about a customer ('Cust said...'); label the customer's view.

Explanation is about how well something was explained when the customer was told, or a failure to explain at handover or when asked in person. A promised call-back or reply that never came is communication; an unexplained or unexpected charge is billing. Do not add explanation on top of those.
Waiting, including on hold, is timeliness; not being answered or called back is communication.
Do not infer a theme from the absence of a problem ('nothing to chase up') unless the customer is clearly commenting on that aspect.
Each theme takes one sentiment. If the customer is both positive and negative about the same theme, record the one that dominates.
